info.name: UrbanStep E-Commerce API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the UrbanStep backend — auth (customer + staff RBAC), products, cart, checkout (Paystack + COD), coupons, refunds, reviews, currency, and webhooks.

## Setup
1. Import the companion `UrbanStep.postman_environment.json` and select it (top-right environment dropdown).
2. Set `baseUrl` (defaults to `http://localhost:5000`).
3. Run **Auth > Register** or **Auth > Login** first — these auto-save `userAccessToken`/`userRefreshToken` into the environment via a test script, so every subsequent authenticated request just works.
4. For admin/staff endpoints, run **Staff Auth > Staff Login** (seeded superadmin credentials from your `.env`'s ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD on first server boot) to populate `staffAccessToken`.
5. Requests are ordered so running a folder top-to-bottom tells a coherent story (e.g. Products: add → list → single → update; Orders: place → mine → track).

## Notes
- Bearer tokens are read from environment variables (`{{userAccessToken}}` / `{{staffAccessToken}}`) — no manual copy-pasting needed after login.
- `productId`, `orderId`, `couponId` etc. are auto-captured from create responses into environment variables for use in later requests in the same folder.
- The Paystack webhook request is included for reference/documentation but can't be meaningfully triggered from Postman — it requires a valid HMAC signature computed with your live `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY`, which Paystack itself computes when it calls your server.

request.description: Creates a customer account. Password must be 8+ chars with uppercase, lowercase, and a symbol. Sends a welcome + verification email if SMTP is configured.
Customer login. Locks the account for ACCOUNT_LOCK_MINUTES after MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS failures.

Requires a real Google ID token, which Postman cannot generate on its own (it comes from Google's Identity Services JS SDK running in a browser after a real Google sign-in). To test this endpoint directly: sign in via the actual frontend's 'Continue with Google' button, open browser devtools -> Network tab, find the request to /api/user/google, and copy the idToken it sent — paste that into the googleIdToken environment variable here. Included for completeness/documentation.
Rotates the refresh token and issues a new short-lived access token.
Revokes all other sessions on success.
Always returns success whether or not the account exists (no email enumeration).
Get the token from the reset email (or server logs in dev if SMTP isn't configured).
Revokes every session/device for this account.
Same credentials as your backend .env ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD (seeds a superadmin on first server boot).
No auth required. Supports category/subCategory/brand/gender/bestseller/search/currency filters + pagination. Cached (Redis) for 60s when REDIS_URL is configured.

multipart/form-data. Attach real image files to image1..image4 in Postman's form-data body editor (the collection defines the field but Postman requires you to browse/attach a file manually per environment).

exec: if (data.success && data.coupon) { pm.environment.set('couponId', data.coupon._id); pm.environment.set('couponCode', data.coupon.code); }

request.description: Returns the discount amount without redeeming it — use to show 'You saved ₦X' before checkout.

idempotencyKey uses Postman's {{$guid}} dynamic variable — generates a fresh UUID per send, so re-sending this request intentionally creates a NEW order (as a real new checkout attempt would). To test idempotency itself, hardcode the same string across two sends instead.
Response includes `paystackAuthorizationUrl` — open it in a browser to complete a real (or Paystack test-mode) payment. The order is marked paid only via the webhook, not this response.
No auth required — set trackingNumber after an admin assigns one via 'Update Order Status'.

Cannot be meaningfully triggered from Postman: this endpoint requires a valid `x-paystack-signature` header, an HMAC-SHA512 of the raw request body computed with your PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY — Paystack computes this when it calls your server for real. Included here for documentation/reference only. To test locally, use Paystack's CLI/dashboard 'send test webhook' feature against a tunneled URL (e.g. ngrok), not this Postman request.
